target_customer: US consumers with thin or no credit files, mainly younger and underserved people, paying a membership fee
problem: People with no credit history cannot get credit and so cannot build a score. Altro lent a small line of credit usable only on subscriptions and reported payments to the credit bureaus; earlier it reported rent.
business_model: Consumer subscription membership with a restricted credit line and bureau reporting

founders.name: Michael Broughton
education: University of Southern California (the founders' notice says the company began among USC students)
founders.background_notes: Background not given on the YC page.

founders.name: Ayush Jain
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as a former founder and CTO.

technical_complexity.rationale: Needed bank partnership, card issuing and bureau reporting integrations, which are standard fintech engineering with compliance overhead.

defensibility.rationale: Depends on a sponsor bank and bureau reporting access; credit-builder products were easy for rivals to copy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Competitors in credit building grew, and Altro announced it had been acquired; the buyer is not named on its site.

market_need_then: Tens of millions of Americans lacked usable credit files, and the company cited 68 million people denied credit; credit-builder apps were gaining users in 2020.

branding.domain_note: Uses altro.io; trademark ALTRO filed April 2022 by Perch Credit, Inc.

identity.voice_and_tone: Mission driven, centered on access to credit for women and people of color

branding.brand_signature: Celebrity investors such as Jay-Z's fund Marcy Ventures, Tinashe and Chris Paul used in announcements

rebrands.why: Not stated in sources found; trademark filed April 2022

branding.community_and_virality: Press coverage focused on celebrity backers and Netflix-for-credit hook; no merch found.

brand_strength.rationale: Celebrity investor coverage in Black Enterprise, Afrotech and Business Wire raised visibility, but sources do not show brand-driven growth.

pivots.from: Helping college students build credit using rent, utilities and recurring payments
pivots.to: Credit line restricted to paying subscriptions to build credit
pivots.why: Stated in YC listing; the reason is not given

outcome_analysis: Altro, previously Perch, joined YC in Summer 2020, raised about $22M in total including an $18M round in 2022 and a $4M strategic round in 2024, and expanded to 47 states with a credit builder card. Its site later announced it had been acquired after about seven years; the buyer, date and terms are not public in sources found, so the outcome quality is unknown.
notes: Total raised $22M is stated by the company's 2024 release. The 2022 $18M round is from Built In and a press release headline; lead investor Pendulum as reported by Built In. One aggregator says a major financial institution acquired it in 2024, unverified and unsupported by the company site. No dated 2020 competitor sources were found. The 2024 investor split among rounds is not stated, so investors are indicative.
